name: Prague
title: Prague in December
lead: Three days on foot, away from the crowds: a library tower, quiet gardens, hill-top sunsets, local pubs and jazz cellars. The sun sets before 16:00, so the day is for sights and the evening for markets and bars.
facts: Sunrise around 7:50, sunset around 15:50. The best light is around 15:00. All times are Prague time, one hour behind Bulgarian time.
Usually between −2 and 3 °C. Bring warm shoes with a non-slip sole; the cobblestones are slippery.

The main markets (Old Town Square and Wenceslas Square) usually run from 28 November to 6 January, 10:00–22:00; one guide says 20 November, so check prague.eu. The smaller ones close on 24 December: Náměstí Míru from 20 November, Náměstí Republiky from 25 November, Tylovo náměstí from 26 November. Each evening in this plan is a different market, and dinner and the bar come after it.

Wallenstein Garden and Vrtba Garden are open only from about April to October, and the Letná beer garden is seasonal. This plan avoids them. Vojan Gardens stay open, but only until 16:00 in December. The Petřín funicular was closed from September 2024 and was due to reopen in 2026; check whether it runs.
Cocktail bars fill up after 21:00, and some stop taking reservations around then. Book a table in advance. Most are open until 01:00–03:00.
On 24, 25 and 26 December many restaurants and sights have shorter hours or are closed. Check ahead.
Czech koruna (CZK). Some small places accept cash only.

days.title: Quiet Old Town, Josefov and a sunset from Letná
days.theme: Start before the crowds, find a few secret corners in the Old Town, watch the sun go down over the bridges from Letná hill, then end in a cocktail bar.

stops.name: Charles Bridge at first light
stops.d: Sunrise is around 7:50. In winter the bridge is almost empty in the early morning, unlike at midday. Walk to the middle and back, then turn towards the Old Town.

stops.name: Infinity Book Tower (Idiom) in the Municipal Library
stops.d: A round tower of books, built by Matej Krén in the library hall at Mariánské náměstí. It is free to see and went viral on TikTok and Instagram. Sources disagree on the opening times: most give Tuesday to Friday from 9:00 and Monday from 13:00, and the weekend hours conflict, so check the library website. The queue is about 30 minutes off-season.
stops.q: Idiom Infinity Book Tower Municipal Library Prague

stops.name: Coffee or breakfast on Valentinská
stops.d: Three places on one street, 3 minutes from the square.

opts.s: coffee
coffee and brunch
breakfast all day

stops.name: Josefov, the Jewish Quarter
stops.d: Pařížská street and the old synagogues from outside. The museums are paid and closed on Saturday.

stops.name: Lunch where locals eat
stops.d: A pub, a butcher counter and a cheap canteen, all within ten minutes of each other. Come before 12:00; there are queues.

opts.s: Czech food and draught beer
butcher shop with a few standing tables; quick meat lunch (check the hours)
cheap Czech canteen lunch that locals queue for

stops.name: Ungelt courtyard and the passages around Old Town Square
stops.d: Walk through the Týn courtyard (Ungelt), the old merchants' yard behind the Týn Church, and the arcades around the square. One local guide also lists the Hrzánská Arcade, reopened in 2024. All are free and much quieter than the square itself.

stops.name: Sunset from the Letná terrace
stops.d: Walk across the Čechův bridge (about 20 minutes) and climb the stairs to Letná. The terrace near the Hanavský pavilion frames the bridges, the river and the Old Town roofs; the sun sets at about 15:50. The Letná beer garden is closed in winter, and the park is big enough that it rarely feels crowded.

stops.name: Christmas market on Wenceslas Square
stops.d: The other big market of the city, on the boulevard below the National Museum: mulled wine, sausages and chimney cakes, lit up after dark. It usually runs from 28 November to 6 January, 10:00–22:00. In the 2025/26 season only the lower part of the square hosted it because of renovation, so check. About 15 minutes' walk from the Old Town.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.d: Two are in the Old Town, one is a famous literary pub. Book ahead, or come early for the pub.

opts.s: traditional setting
historic Old Town pub, a haunt of the writer Bohumil Hrabal; popular, so go early (check the opening hours)
right on the square, Czech food

stops.name: A drink after dinner
stops.d: Three cocktail bars within ten minutes of each other. Book a table in advance: one guide says Hemingway Bar stops taking reservations at 21:00 and has a queue by 22:00 at weekends. AnonymouS Bar also has a line most Saturdays.

opts.s: classic cocktail bar, open from the early evening; reserve a table
medieval cellar under the Hotel U Prince; enter through the hotel lobby
opts.q: Black Angel's Bar Prague U Prince

opts.s: hacker-themed bar with a puzzle menu, open until 02:00

days.title: Castle, Strahov, Petřín and a garden with peacocks
days.theme: Start at the castle before the groups, take the quiet back lanes to Strahov, walk up Petřín, finish in the Malá Strana gardens and listen to jazz in a cellar.

stops.name: Prague Castle
stops.d: Be at the second courtyard before 9:00. The grounds are free from 6 to 22, paid buildings are open from 9 to 16. A Circuit B ticket is from 250 CZK, Circuit A from 350 CZK, valid for two days. Tuesday and Wednesday are quietest.

stops.name: Nový Svět, the quiet lane behind the castle
stops.d: A short walk from Loreta Square, a cobbled lane of small houses under the Černín Palace gardens. It is a residential street, so stay quiet; it is usually very peaceful.

stops.name: Strahov Library and Monastery
stops.d: The Baroque library is open daily from 9:00 to 17:00 and closed on 24 and 25 December. On the normal ticket you look into the halls from the doorway; the price is about 220 CZK, but guides quote 180–350 CZK.

stops.name: Lunch at the monastery or in a Hradčany pub
stops.d: A monastery brewery and a very cheap local pub, both within ten minutes of Strahov, and a restaurant on the way down.

opts.s: own St Norbert beer, about 110 CZK for half a litre
cheap local pub by Loreta; profits go to a school; reviews are mixed on cleanliness
opts.q: U Černého vola Prague Loretánské náměstí

opts.s: restaurant under the castle

stops.name: Petřín hill and tower
stops.d: Walk up from Strahov through the park, about 15 minutes. The tower is open from 10:00 to 18:00 in December (city website; 10:00–15:00 on 24 December). The funicular was closed from September 2024 and was due to reopen in 2026; check whether it runs, or walk.

stops.name: Kampa, Vojan Gardens and Prague's narrowest street
stops.d: On the way down from Petřín, cross Kampa island and the John Lennon Wall. Then Vojan Gardens: the oldest partly preserved garden in Prague, free, with peacocks and a chapel built like a stalactite cave. Enter from U Lužického semináře. In December it is open only from 8:00 to 16:00, so go in by 15:30. The gap in the wall nearby is Prague's narrowest street, which went viral on TikTok; it has a traffic light because only one person fits at a time.

stops.name: Sunset on the Malá Strana bank by the Čertovka
stops.d: The sun sets at about 15:50. Stand by the Čertovka mill stream or on the bank by the bridge and watch the sky over the castle.

stops.name: Christmas market on Old Town Square
stops.d: Walk back over the lit Charles Bridge (about 20 minutes) to the biggest market of the city: mulled wine (svařák), sausage, potato pancakes, baked bread and trdelník, with the tree and the lit towers. It usually runs from 28 November to 6 January, 10:00–22:00 (one guide says it opens on 20 November; check prague.eu).
stops.q: Old Town Square Christmas market Prague

stops.name: Dinner in Malá Strana
stops.d: Walk back over the bridge. Three places in Malá Strana: a grand café-restaurant at the foot of Petřín and two Czech restaurants.

opts.s: grand classic café-restaurant at the foot of Petřín
Czech food, near Újezd
Czech food on the square

stops.name: Jazz or a late drink
stops.d: Three bars within ten minutes of each other. U Malého Glena is a small blues and jazz cellar; check the programme and start time.

opts.s: small jazz and blues cellar; some nights free entry
long-running bar with many spirits, open until 03:00
courtyard café-bar, open until midnight

days.title: Vinohrady, Žižkov and the Vítkov sunset
days.theme: A local day away from the centre: a neighbourhood market, a vineyard park, the TV tower, a sunset on Vítkov hill and the pubs of Žižkov.

stops.name: Breakfast or coffee in Vinohrady
stops.d: A sourdough bakery, a classic breakfast café and a brunch spot, all in Vinohrady. Pekárna Praktika has no sign outside, mills its own flour and sells out early, so go first.

opts.s: sourdough bakery with heritage-grain loaves; open Tuesday to Saturday, sells out within a couple of hours
café open since 1995; known for breakfast and pancakes
brunch all day, from 8:00 (9:00 at weekends)

stops.name: Church of St Ludmila at náměstí Míru
stops.d: The Neo-Gothic church on Vinohrady's main square, with two tall spires. The square is the centre of the district; the market here is in the evening.
stops.q: Church of St Ludmila Náměstí Míru Prague

stops.name: Havlíčkovy sady (Grébovka) and its vineyard
stops.d: A landscaped hill park with a vineyard, a wooden gazebo and a wine cellar. In winter the vines are bare and the park is quiet. Opening times of the cellar and the grotto in winter are not confirmed.

stops.name: Lunch in Vinohrady
stops.d: Three Czech places in Vinohrady. They are mostly listed in local guides, so check that they are open.

opts.s: Czech food, well rated
modern Czech food
Czech pub food and a good beer list

stops.name: Riegrovy sady
stops.d: A hill park above the city with views of the castle. It is a favourite spot for sunset among locals and is busy on warm evenings; in December it is much quieter. Walk through on your way to Žižkov.

stops.name: Sunset on Vítkov hill
stops.d: A local guide calls it a favourite for the best sunset panorama over the city, free and usually without crowds. The statue of Jan Žižka on horseback is one of the largest in the world. Opening times of the National Monument building are not confirmed, so plan on the outdoor view.

stops.name: Žižkov TV Tower
stops.d: The 1980s tower with giant crawling babies on its legs. The observation deck costs about 350 CZK; guides give opening times from 9:00 to 23:30 or midnight, so check before you go. The view at dusk is good.

stops.name: Christmas market on náměstí Míru
stops.d: The local Christmas market on Vinohrady's main square, usually from 20 November to 24 December, about 10:00–20:00, so it closes after Christmas Eve. It is smaller and more local than the Old Town market. About 20 minutes' walk from the TV Tower.

stops.name: Dinner in Žižkov
stops.d: A 20-minute walk from the market. Three Czech pubs and halls in Žižkov, the district with the most pubs per head in Prague (a claim locals make). Czech beer is cheap here.

opts.s: neighbourhood pub just under the TV Tower; old-timers and young locals
casual Czech beer hall, well rated on Tripadvisor
hearty Czech dinner

stops.name: Žižkov bars
stops.d: Three very different bars within ten minutes of each other. U Vystřelenýho Oka opens at 16:30 and the beer costs about 45 CZK; Bukowski's is a cocktail bar open from 19:00; Tiki Taky is a tiki bar that stays open late.

opts.n: U Vystřelenýho Oka, U Božích bojovníků 3
opts.s: legendary Žižkov pub under the Žižka statue
cocktail bar, a favourite of locals and expats
tiki bar, open late
